A covariate balance table

Source: R/panel_causal.R
baltab.Rd

Means of each covariate in the treated and comparison groups, their standardised mean difference, and Welch's test, optionally weighted (after matching or weighting).

Usage

baltab(data, grp, covs, w = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit.

grp

Column name of the 0/1 group (1 = treated).

covs

Column names to compare.

w

Optional column name of weights.

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_balance: covariate, meantrtd, meanctl, smd, p_value.

Details

The standardised mean difference is \((\bar x_1 - \bar x_0) / s_1\) with \(s_1\) the unweighted standard deviation in the treated group (the convention for the effect on the treated, so that it does not move when weights change the comparison group); \(|SMD| < 0.1\) is the usual threshold for balance. With weights the means are weighted and the test uses the weighted variances and Kish's effective sample sizes.

References

Welch BL (1947). The generalization of ‘Student's’ problem when several different population variances are involved. Biometrika 34(1-2):28-35. doi:10.1093/biomet/34.1-2.28

Examples

d <- data.frame(t = rep(0:1, each = 50),
                age = c(stats::rnorm(50, 30), stats::rnorm(50, 33)))
baltab(d, "t", "age")
#>   covariate meantrtd  meanctl      smd      p_value
#> 1       age 32.80419 30.09459 2.747349 1.777265e-26
